conflict_policy.why: name/version/bin/scripts are the Lattice distribution contract. Take upstream only for genuinely new runtime dependencies, by hand.
EXTRACTION_VERSION gates the incremental re-extraction heal. Both sides bump it independently, so the two values can name different output — the merged value must be higher than either, never a pick.

KERNEL_ABI_VERSION collides: upstream v2 is a 40-byte ref row with a flags byte; Lattice layers extraJson on top for 48. Same number, different layout — the loader's version check would pass while decode mis-reads. After a sync that touches the layout, advance Lattice's number PAST upstream's, and move layout.ts in the same commit.
Lattice ships no standalone installer (BUNDLING.md). Upstream installer targets do not apply.
telemetry is disabled in Lattice; upstream's design notes describe a surface we do not run.
describes the Lattice-owned sensor, not the upstream product.
path_map applies (codegraph-kernel -> lattice-sensor-kernel) and Lattice stages prebuilds where its own loader looks.

Both sides number migrations independently. Lattice databases in the field carry Lattice's numbers (9-12 as of 2026-09-30), so upstream's migrations are carried ABOVE the highest Lattice number (upstream 9-11 became 13-15) and CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION is the highest carried number. Never reuse a number a field database may already record.
EDGE_KINDS order is the wire contract with src/types.ts. When both sides append a kind, append Lattice's first (invokes, then navigates as of 2026-09-30) in BOTH files, and bump the array length.

Lattice keeps one fixed state path (.lattice/sensor) with no LATTICE_SENSOR_DIR override and no per-host variant; other Lattice components address the index by that path. Upstream's WSL-on-Windows-drive sibling (#995) is not taken: latticeSensorRelativeDirFor returns the fixed path, and the WSL constants exist only so upstream's WSL diagnostics compile (they stay dormant).

Take upstream's commands except: install/uninstall/upgrade stay refused (BUNDLING.md, ADR 0049/0059), and no dynamic import of ../installer or ../upgrade. callers/callees take upstream's per-definition implementation (#1512/#1639/#1473) PLUS Lattice's contract used by src/sensor-adapter.mjs, todo-structure-source-adapter and seam-cost: --exact-path with exactPath/exactResolution, and edgeKind/valueRef/valueWrite on every listed node. The root adapter accepts upstream's did-you-mean suffix on 'Symbol "X" not found'.
Lattice's isRunnableTestFile and upstream's isTestPath are the same narrow test-suite check; upstream's structure is taken and isRunnableTestFile is kept as an alias.

A daemon hello without the -lattice. version marker is a foreign product (ADR 0049 Decision 5③) and fails the session closed. Upstream version-mismatch fixtures must use a marked version and the `sensor` hello field to exercise the same-product path.

Upstream moved its config to vitest.config.mts + vitest.workspace.mts. Lattice uses vitest.config.mts alone (the workspace needs the Svelte plugin for ui-package.test.ts) and keeps an exclude list for suites whose surface Lattice does not operate: install/update machinery, the Svelte viewer build, and the WSL sibling state dir. Those files are still synced so the next sync sees upstream's changes.

Lattice keeps ui/ sources (its pure-TS models are exercised by engine tests) but does not build or ship the viewer. The viewer build runs only when package.json defines build:ui; a non-JSON package.json (the isolated fixtures) falls back to whether ui/ exists.

notes: absorbed_at records where sensor/ came from. It never moves, and it is NOT the merge base.

synced_at IS the 3-way merge base, and it advances ONLY when a sync lands with zero unresolved conflicts. Using absorbed_at as the base instead makes every hand-resolved conflict re-conflict on the next sync — a resolution would have no way to reach a settled state. A partially applied sync must leave the marker untouched, or the next run silently skips what was never merged.
A sync target must be a descendant of synced_at. Pointing --ref at an older commit would move the marker backwards while the tree stays new.

The rename to LATTICE_SENSOR_* / lattice-sensor is carried as an ordinary local change: git resolves it as ours, so no rename rules are needed. Do not add textual substitution to the sync path — the rename is selective (some CODEGRAPH_* names are deliberately kept) and cannot be reproduced by rules.
lattice_only paths are never deleted by a sync even when absent upstream.

conflict_policy exists so a resolution is decided once, not re-litigated every sync. When a conflict is resolved by hand, add the path and the reason here — an entry that only says 'ours' without a why is worse than none.

After a sync, upstream's NEW lines carry upstream names (CodeGraph/codegraph/CODEGRAPH_*). Run scripts/upstream-rename.mjs --write over sensor code (and --prose over sensor/docs) BEFORE resolving conflicts, so both sides of a hunk carry the same names, then fix what build and tests expose. src/, __tests__/, scripts/, the kernel and docs/ keep zero codegraph mentions (test/lattice-sensor-runtime.test.mjs).
